subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Should maintainers change the OpenAI Realtime to Twilio output policy now, and should the chosen fix be gain headroom, codec/output-format, pacing/backpressure instrumentation, or a narrower live-proven repair?
rationale: The source path is clear but the reported clipping is a live telephony artifact, and several plausible fixes would change shared realtime voice behavior without proof of the failing layer.

options.title: Require live diagnostics first
options.body: Collect current-main Twilio/OpenAI audio and queue/level evidence before choosing the owner boundary or changing output audio policy.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow codec/pacing experiment
options.body: Authorize a bounded branch that adds diagnostics and one opt-in candidate fix, with live proof required before merge.

options.title: Defer until repro artifact arrives
options.body: Keep the issue open but avoid implementation work until the reporter or maintainer can provide a current audio sample or call transcript.

recommendation.title: Require live diagnostics first
recommendation.body: Collect current-main Twilio/OpenAI audio and queue/level evidence before choosing the owner boundary or changing output audio policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent maintainer-authored OpenAI realtime and voice-call output-path refactors make this the strongest available routing owner for the product/audio-policy choice.
